response.sql: WITH c AS (SELECT o.timespan AS time_in_force, COUNT(*) AS record_count FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT time_in_force, record_count, record_count * 1.0 / SUM(record_count) OVER () AS share FROM c) SELECT time_in_force, record_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_diff_from_avg FROM s ORDER BY time_in_force

assumptions.assumption: Records are counted per riskandmargin row after an inner join to orders, so an order with several records counts once per record and unmatched records are dropped.
The difference is share minus the simple average of the per-group shares, which equals 1/number of groups. The result is signed and unrounded.
Matched orders whose timespan is NULL form their own group and count toward the total and the average. If there are none, this has no effect.
